transcript.text: "Not working properly" can mean a few different things. The most common simple cause is that the child lock (often indicated by a key or padlock symbol) has been accidentally activated, which disables the controls. Another possibility is that a specific heating element, coil, or induction module for one zone has failed. To help me guide you correctly, could you tell me if the hob has a child lock symbol on the control panel? Also, is it just one specific cooking zone that isn't working, or are all of them affected?
It's just the rear right one that's not heating. I don't see a padlock or key symbol on it, the other three zones work fine.

Since only the rear right zone is affected and the others work fine, we can rule out a general power supply issue. The two main possibilities are that the pan you're using isn't suitable for that specific zone (common with induction hobs), or there is a fault with the heating element/coil itself. Please try placing a pan that you know works on the other zones onto the rear right one. Does it heat up? Also, do you know if your hob is an induction type (uses magnets) or a ceramic/halogen type?
It's a ceramic one, flat glass top, with touch controls. Same pan on the other zones heats fine but on the rear right it doesn't glow red or get warm at all, even though the display shows the number.

The most likely cause is that the ceramic heating coil itself has failed internally and needs replacing; less commonly, the relay on the main board controlling that specific zone may have failed. To help me identify the correct replacement part for your hob, could you please provide the make and model number? This is usually found on a sticker on the underside of the unit or on the guarantee card.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
It's a Zanussi. I can't find the full model number, but the manual cover says it starts with ZHRN. Is that enough?

That model hint helps confirm it's likely a Zanussi ZHRN series, but since you can't reach the sticker right now we don't need it for this diagnosis. Based on your description—a single zone showing power but not heating while others work—the most likely cause is that the radiant heating element under the glass has failed internally. Because replacing this part involves removing the heavy glass top and dealing with mains electricity, it is not safe to attempt yourself; you should call a qualified appliance engineer to replace the element.
